questions.question: Why should only one module (config.py) read environment variables?
options: Python only allows one module to read os.environ
So every setting and its default lives in one place, and secrets can be masked consistently
questions.explanation: Scattered env reads mean conflicting defaults and secrets leaking through ad-hoc prints. One config module fixes both.

questions.question: What's the difference between tests/ and evals/ in this layout?
options: Tests are deterministic offline checks of the code (scripted model); evals run real tasks on a real model and score behavior
Tests use real models; evals use fakes
questions.explanation: Tests check code correctness on every commit. Evals measure agent behavior, which varies and needs a real model.

questions.question: Why keep prompts as files in agent/prompts/ instead of strings in code?
options: Prompt changes show up as clear diffs, get reviewed like code, and can be compared in evals
questions.explanation: Prompts change agent behavior as much as code does, so they deserve versioning and review.

questions.question: Why does the generated CLI fall back to a scripted model when AGENT_BASE_URL is unset?
options: So a fresh project runs immediately with zero setup, and CI never needs a model or key
questions.explanation: Offline-by-default makes the project runnable and testable anywhere; a real model is one env var away.

questions.question: The same eval case failed in one run and passed in the next. What should you conclude?
options: Model behavior varies; run each case several times and report a pass rate instead of a single pass/fail
The second run is the true result
Use a scripted model for evals
questions.explanation: Real-model evals are noisy. Repeated runs and pass rates turn anecdotes into measurements.

questions.question: The scaffolder's tests run the generated project's tests, CLI and evals. Why go that far?
options: Generated code can be broken even when templates look fine; only executing it proves the scaffold works
questions.explanation: This lesson's own tests caught a template that generated a syntax error, which only running the output reveals.
